content.overview: If the number of members falls below seven in a public company or two in a private company, and the company carries on business for more than six months, every continuing member who knows of it is severally liable for debts contracted after those six months.
content.glance: If the number of members falls below seven in a public company or two in a private company, and the company carries on business for more than six months, every continuing member who knows of it is severally liable for debts contracted after those six months.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 3A (Members severally liable). If the number of members falls below seven in a public company or two in a private company, and the company carries on business for more than six months, every continuing member who knows of it is severally liable for debts contracted after those six months. The section applies only to the persons, companies, and transactions it names. A filing, approval, or penalty arises only where the section or a rule under it says so. It does not create a power that is reserved to another section or to the Tribunal. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: Explanation
sections.body: Section 3A was inserted by the Companies (Amendment) Act, 2017. It does not dissolve the company. It imposes personal liability on members who know of the shortfall and continue the business. One person companies are outside the two-member floor.
